digest.headline: Today's World Briefing: Trump’s meddling in Huang scandal reignites voter angst over tech’s outsized political power
digest.dek: What 7 major outlets covered for Wednesday, November 25, ranked by how widely each story was reported.
digest.overview: 195 distinct stories ran across 7 major outlets in the latest news cycle. The most widely covered was “Trump’s meddling in Huang scandal reignites voter angst over tech’s outsized political power”, reported by 5 outlets (BBC, CNBC, CNN, NYT, WSJ). It was followed by “Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy” and “U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU”. Technology dominated the agenda, accounting for 2 of the top 8 stories. Words that kept coming up: huang, trump, scandal, jensen, nvidia, apologiz.

paragraphs.title: Trump’s meddling in Huang scandal reignites voter angst over tech’s outsized political power
paragraphs.text: In technology, CNBC reports: Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang after pressure from Trump is intensifying bipartisan scrutiny of tech companies' ties to the administration. Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value. The reinstatement of Jensen Huang atop Nvidia, following pressure from President Trump, shattered norms for corporate governance.

paragraphs.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy
paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, NBC News reports: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. A day after returning to his company, Mr. Huang acknowledged that he had violated Nvidia’s code of conduct and “made some terrible mistakes.” The Nvidia co-founder thanked the Trump administration while addressing staff the day after he was reinstated as CEO.

paragraphs.title: U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU
paragraphs.text: On the business side, CNBC reports: The new levies seek to counter foreign trade practices deemed unfair, discriminatory, or burdensome to U.S. commerce. Trump proposes a new wave of tariffs on China, E.U. The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.

paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, WSJ reports: Plus: Malaysia finds no record of U.S.-sanctioned firm, Jensen Huang’s comeback collides with lawmakers demanding answers.

paragraphs.title: Army set to detonate a cache of lead explosives, sending toxic plume across Iowa
paragraphs.text: On the international stage, NBC News reports: The Army plans to detonate a stockpile of unstable lead azide explosives in Iowa on Wednesday morning. The toxic dust plume is expected to travel for miles. Residents of Middletown, which adjoins an Army facility where dangerous chemicals will be detonated Wednesday, are taping up their doors and getting ready to flee.

paragraphs.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia lands in Spain a ‘free man’ after deportation battle
paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, NBC News reports: Kilmar Abrego Garcia has landed in Spain after leaving the United States at the end of a closely watched and controversial deportation battle that became a symbol for the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported from the United States last year, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday, ending a 20-month legal fight.

paragraphs.title: Stock futures tumble as Nvidia leads AI sell-off, data shows inflation picking up: Live updates
paragraphs.text: On the markets front, CNBC reports: Wall Street is coming off a losing session for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite. Shares have veered wildly for days, pushed and pulled by the drama at Nvidia and the rise and fall of Anthropic’s stock after its blockbuster public offering.
